column5: A structure nearer the trunk or point of attachment is described by this directional adjective.

Lying face downward is described by this adjective, also used for a hand turned palm-down.

A substance or infectious agent originating outside the body is described by this adjective.

Quiet breathing at a normal resting rate and depth is described by this term.
Difficulty swallowing is this term, distinct from painful swallowing.
Pain during swallowing is specified by this term beginning with a pain-related prefix.
Weak or poorly coordinated speech muscles can cause this articulation disorder even when language formulation remains intact.
Impaired coordination of voluntary movement is described by this term.
Tingling, prickling, or pins-and-needles sensations are grouped under this sensory term.
Blood visible or detected in urine is called this.
A laboratory count showing unusually many white blood cells is described by this term.
An unusually low platelet count is described by this term.
Enlargement of the liver is expressed by this single compound term.
Enlargement of the spleen is expressed by this parallel compound term.
Enlarged lymph nodes are collectively described by this term.
Breathlessness that worsens when lying flat and improves on sitting up is called this.
A temporary worsening of a chronic condition's signs or symptoms is called this.
Residual impairment or another lasting consequence after an illness or injury is this.
Early symptoms that precede the characteristic phase of an illness make up this stage.
A surgically created or naturally occurring connection between two vessels or hollow structures is this.
Abnormal narrowing of a passage such as a valve, vessel, or spinal canal is this.
Complete blockage or closure of a vessel or passage is described by this term.
Tissue death caused by prolonged loss of blood supply produces this localized lesion.
Restoring blood flow can paradoxically add oxidative and inflammatory damage through this process.
Unregulated cell death accompanied by membrane breakdown and inflammation is broadly termed this.
Replacement of one mature cell type by another mature cell type in response to stress is this adaptation.
Disordered cell growth with atypical size, shape, and organization is called this, especially in epithelia.
An increase in the number of cells enlarging a tissue is this adaptation.
An increase in individual cell size, rather than cell number, is this adaptation.
A decrease in tissue size from shrinking cells or loss of cells is this process.
Complete failure of an organ to form during embryonic development is described by this term.
Failure of a tissue to develop despite the presence of a rudimentary precursor is called this.
Incomplete development leaving an organ smaller or less mature than usual is this.
Histologically normal tissue found in an abnormal anatomical site is described by this term.
An organ protruding through an opening in the wall that normally contains it is this general condition.
A finding so strongly characteristic of one disease that its presence can establish the diagnosis is described by this adjective.
Pain perceived at a site distant from its actual source, such as shoulder discomfort from diaphragmatic irritation, is this.
A skin region supplied mainly by sensory fibers from one spinal nerve root is called this.
Pain, weakness, or sensory change caused by dysfunction of a spinal nerve root is broadly called this.
Cramping limb discomfort brought on by exertion and relieved by rest is described by this gait-related term.
A grating or crackling sensation felt or heard when tissues move is called this.
Rumbling or gurgling intestinal sounds have this onomatopoeic plural name.
A whooshing vascular sound heard with a stethoscope is this, from the French word for noise.
A vibration felt by palpation over turbulent blood flow is this tactile counterpart of a vascular sound.
Rhythmic involuntary oscillation of the eyes is called this.
Unequal pupil sizes are described by this term.
Forward protrusion of the eyeball is this term, also called proptosis.
A bluish discoloration of skin or mucosa caused by increased deoxygenated hemoglobin is this sign.
Redness of skin produced by capillary dilation is described by this term.
Generalized, severe edema involving subcutaneous tissues throughout the body is called this.
Profound weight and muscle loss associated with chronic illness is called this wasting state.
Tiny nonblanching red or purple spots caused by bleeding into skin are called these.

A netlike mottled reddish-blue skin pattern is described by this Latin term.
Spoon-shaped concavity of the fingernails is this morphology.
Separation of the nail plate from its underlying bed is called this.
A lipid-rich yellowish deposit in skin or tendons is called this.
Persistent sensation of needing to empty the bowel or bladder despite little output is this symptom.
Bulky, pale, oily stool caused by excess fat is described by this term.
Black, tarry stool containing digested blood is called this.
Passage of visibly fresh blood from the lower gastrointestinal tract is called this.
Coughing up blood originating from the respiratory tract is called this.

Two small masses on cables spin outward after launch and are then released, reducing a probe's rotation through this technique.

Commands stored onboard and executed at predetermined times allow distant probes to operate through communication delays using this approach.

column5: A scheduled parliamentary period in which legislators directly challenge ministers is this accountability practice.
The constitutionally specified duration for which an elected official holds office is this interval.
column6: What is a term of office?

column5: A substitute temporarily exercises royal authority when a monarch is a minor or unable to perform official duties in this arrangement.
The division of taxing, borrowing, and spending responsibilities among levels of government is studied under this branch of federal arrangements.
Ultimate constitutional authority rests with the central government, even if it delegates power locally, in this state structure.
A chamber designed to represent provinces, states, or regions at the national level is this kind of legislative body.
column6: What is a federal second chamber?

column5: Two chambers possessing roughly equal constitutional authority create this balance between houses.
Cabinet members emerging from and remaining part of the legislative majority creates this institutional relationship.
A specialized tribunal empowered to decide constitutional disputes is this institution.
The broader idea that public authority is created and limited by a fundamental legal framework is this.
Moving ministers among portfolios without changing the governing party is called this executive reorganization.
In Canada, direct bargaining among the prime minister, premiers, and their cabinets exemplifies this approach to intergovernmental relations.
A ministry's continued tenure depends on maintaining this relationship with the elected chamber.
The mathematical conversion of votes into legislative seats is broadly called this process.
A nonbinding public vote used to gauge opinion on a major issue is often termed this.
Changing a constitution through its formally prescribed procedure is this legal act.
In this semi-proportional system, each voter receives fewer votes than the number of seats available, allowing cohesive minorities to gain representation.
Legislators vote through repeated rounds, eliminating the lowest candidate each time until someone wins a majority, in this method.
Assigning points to each rank and electing the highest total scorer follows this eighteenth-century voting rule.
Ranked first choices are counted, then successively lower rankings are added until a candidate crosses a majority under this method.
Only registered party members may choose that party's nominee in this nominating contest.
Voters may choose which party's nominating contest to join without prior party registration in this contest.
Voters choose among all candidates on one preliminary ballot, with top finishers advancing regardless of party, in this format.
column6: What is a nonpartisan blanket primary?

column5: A geographically defined body of voters represented by an elected legislator is this electoral unit.
Selection of an officeholder by representatives rather than voters directly uses this electoral mechanism.
Delegates gathering formally to select a party's candidates use this nominating institution.
Citizens place a proposed law or constitutional change on the ballot by gathering signatures under this device.
Citizens unable to reach a polling station may cast a ballot remotely before election day through this method.
Rules determining which candidates or parties may appear on voting papers are collectively called this.
Requiring a candidate to pay money that is refunded after reaching a vote threshold uses this nomination device.
A law reserving a minimum share of candidacies for women establishes this representational mechanism.
column6: What is a candidate gender quota?

column5: Public reporting of political donations and spending implements this campaign-finance safeguard.
A multimember council collectively performs head-of-state and head-of-government functions in this executive arrangement exemplified by Switzerland.
An elected local council appoints a professional administrator to run daily operations under this municipal structure.
In this contrasting semi-presidential subtype, both president and parliament can dismiss the prime minister.
A head of state ending a legislature's term and triggering an election exercises this authority.
A legislature may reenact a law despite a constitutional-court ruling when a constitution provides this political response.
Final authority to settle constitutional meaning rests primarily with courts under this institutional doctrine.
Requiring a supermajority or referendum rather than ordinary legislation makes a constitutional rule this.
A single written instrument consolidating the central rules of government in this type of constitution.
A central state transfers governing authority to regional bodies without making those powers constitutionally sovereign in this process.
Different constituent regions possess different degrees or kinds of authority under this federal arrangement.
A municipality protected against arbitrary state interference may possess this chartered authority over local affairs.
Both national and subnational governments may legislate in the same policy field when they possess these powers.
Valid national law displacing conflicting subnational law illustrates this doctrine of priority.
A constitution's explicit list of legislative authorities grants these powers.
Electoral rules designed to reward candidates for attracting support across communal divisions follow this integration-oriented model.
Routine bargaining and coordination among national and subnational executives is studied under this broad label.
Voters abandoning a preferred trailing candidate to prevent a less-liked winner exhibit this pressure in plurality elections.
A committee chair able to choose between a proposal and the status quo can exploit sequence and preferences under this spatial model.
With multidimensional majority voting and no stable core, proposal sequences can lead almost anywhere under this result.
Any deterministic voting rule with at least three alternatives that is strategy-proof must be dictatorial, under this theorem.
Lijphart contrasts concentrated executive power and plurality elections in this democratic model with a consensus model.
Broad coalitions, proportionality, and dispersed institutional power characterize this Lijphart model.
This index sums absolute changes in party vote shares between two elections and divides the total by two.
This early disproportionality measure averages the absolute difference between each party's vote and seat shares.
The responsiveness of seat share to a change in vote share is summarized by this electoral quantity.
This normative model expects disciplined parties to offer distinct programs and implement them when elected.
Election victory is sometimes interpreted as voter authorization to carry out a published program under this theory.
Kirchheimer used this term for parties that weaken class or religious ties to appeal broadly across the electorate.
Katz and Mair described established parties increasingly reliant on state resources and mutually protective competition with this label.
column6: What is the cartel party thesis?

column5: Lipset and Rokkan explained durable European party alignments through social divisions such as center-periphery and labor-capital in this approach.
Tsebelis analyzes policy stability by counting actors whose agreement is necessary to change the status quo under this theory.
Institutions can persist because early choices generate increasing returns and make alternative routes costly under this historical concept.
A governing alliance containing no party unnecessary for retaining a legislative majority is this kind of coalition.

column5: Among majority coalitions, one with the smallest total seat count is this more restrictive office-seeking prediction.

The person designated to negotiate and assemble a cabinet after an election has this comparative-politics title.
Coalition partners tend to receive cabinet portfolios roughly proportional to their legislative seats under this empirical regularity.
A small party able to determine which of two larger blocs forms a majority occupies this strategic role.
In spatial voting, the actor whose support changes an otherwise losing proposal into a winning one is this.
Cox and McCubbins argue that majority parties organize legislatures partly to prevent proposals dividing their own members under this theory.
Keeping proposals off the floor is this form of power, distinct from winning votes after debate begins.
An agency's implementation gradually departing from the policy preferences of elected principals is called this.
Bueno de Mesquita and colleagues relate leaders' survival strategies to the size of the group choosing them and the coalition needed to remain in power in this theory.
Dahl used this term for a system combining broad participation with meaningful public contestation.
A constitution may bar amendment of certain foundational commitments through this entrenched provision.
Courts invoking this doctrine hold that even a formally valid amendment can violate a constitution's basic structure.
column6: What is the unconstitutional constitutional amendment doctrine?

column5: The original authority claimed by a people or convention to create a constitutional order is this concept associated with Sieyes.
A democracy may restrict organizations seeking to abolish democratic order under this self-protective doctrine.

column5: The idea that the laws are unchanged under a transformation such as rotation is expressed by this foundational concept.

Electrons lost energy only in fixed amounts while colliding with mercury atoms, supporting discrete atomic levels in this experiment.

Microwave transitions in hydrogen exposed a small separation between two levels Dirac theory had predicted identical in this measurement.
Entangled-photon measurements with changing polarizer settings violated a Bell inequality in these landmark 1980s tests.
Atomic clocks flown around Earth aboard airliners accumulated direction-dependent time differences in this test of relativity.
Two slits producing an interference pattern one detected particle at a time dramatize this classic quantum experiment.
column6: What is the single-particle double-slit experiment?

column5: Aharonov and Bohm predicted that electrons acquire a measurable phase around a shielded magnetic flux even where the local field vanishes.

A hypothetical collection of identically prepared systems represents probabilities in statistical mechanics and is called this.
Fixed energy, volume, and particle number define this isolated-system ensemble.
Fixed temperature, volume, and particle number define this heat-bath ensemble.
A system exchanging both energy and particles with a reservoir is described by this ensemble.
column6: What is the grand canonical ensemble?

column5: Summing Boltzmann weights over available states gives this central function from which equilibrium properties can be derived.
This hypothesis equates long-time averages of an isolated system with averages over its accessible state space.
The exponential of minus energy divided by kT gives this relative equilibrium weight.
A tiny being sorting fast and slow molecules appears to reduce entropy without work in this thought experiment.
Treating identical particles as distinguishable causes a spurious entropy of mixing in this classical puzzle.
Erasing one bit of information must dissipate at least kT times the natural log of two in heat under this principle.
Microscopically different systems can share the same near-critical scaling behavior because they belong to one of these classes.
A power governing how correlation length or heat capacity diverges near a continuous transition is this quantity.
Magnetization distinguishes ordered and disordered phases in a ferromagnet and is an example of this diagnostic quantity.
Fluctuations become correlated over all length scales at a continuous transition, producing this scale-free phenomenon.
Systematically averaging over short-distance detail shows how physical parameters change with scale in this framework.
Assuming uncorrelated incoming molecular velocities, this result shows a kinetic-theory quantity H cannot increase toward equilibrium.
Demanding that phase conventions may vary independently from point to point requires introducing connection fields under this principle.
An ordinary derivative amended with a gauge connection preserves local transformation behavior and has this name.
Photons, gluons, and the W and Z particles mediate interactions as this class of force carrier.
A field acquiring a nonzero vacuum value gives W and Z particles mass without explicitly breaking gauge consistency through this mechanism.
Spontaneously breaking a continuous global symmetry produces a massless excitation under this theorem.
The average value of a field in its lowest-energy state, which may differ from zero, is this quantity.
column6: What is a vacuum expectation value?

column5: A measured interaction strength can vary with energy scale rather than remain fixed, behaving as this kind of parameter.
Quarks interact more weakly at very high momentum transfer through this property of the strong interaction.

Low-energy predictions can be organized without knowing all short-distance details by including every interaction allowed by symmetries in this framework.
This two-point Green function gives the amplitude for a disturbance to travel between spacetime points.
Replacing real time by imaginary time turns oscillatory quantum integrals into Euclidean statistical ones through this analytic continuation.
One scattering amplitude can be related to another by moving a particle between initial and final states while replacing it with its antiparticle under this property.
The combined reversal of charge, spatial parity, and time remains an invariance of local Lorentz-respecting quantum field theories.
Integer-spin particles are bosons and half-integer-spin particles are fermions under this deep connection.
Virtual charged pairs screen electric charge and modify a photon's propagation through this quantum effect.
The maximum information in a region may scale with its boundary area rather than its volume under this principle inspired by black holes.
A gravitational theory in negatively curved spacetime can be equivalent to a lower-dimensional conformal field theory on its boundary in this duality.
Unitary quantum evolution appears to conflict with complete thermal evaporation of a black hole in this puzzle.
column6: What is the black-hole information paradox?

column5: A black hole's thermodynamic entropy equals one quarter of its horizon area in Planck units under this formula.

A classical symmetry may fail after quantization because no regulator preserves it, producing this phenomenon.
